title: Name the reason a solve was refused

blocks.text: A logistics platform logs every solve that MathOpt refuses, and its on-call engineers want one line per refusal: the status code's name and the solver's message. In OR-Tools 9.15 a refusal reaches you as `AttributeError: 'StatusNotOk' object has no attribute 'canonical_code'`, and the real error is on the exception's `__context__`: an object with an integer `code` and a `message`. A later OR-Tools that fixes the bug raises MathOpt's own exception instead, whose message ends with ` (was C++ INVALID_ARGUMENT)` or another code's name.

items: When `error.__context__` has a `code` and a `message`, return the code's name from `CODE_NAMES` (or `"UNKNOWN"` for a code not in it) and that message as it is.
Otherwise, when the error's text ends with ` (was C++ NAME)`, return `NAME` and the text before that suffix.
Otherwise return `"UNKNOWN"` and the error's text, `str(error)`.

blocks.text: `CODE_NAMES` is given: it maps the absl status codes MathOpt uses to their names.

cases.says: a refused HiGHS thread count gives ('INVALID_ARGUMENT', the solver's message without the bracketed code)
an integer model sent to GLOP gives ('INVALID_ARGUMENT', 'Glop does not support integer variables')
a quadratic objective sent to HiGHS gives the code 'UNIMPLEMENTED'
a ValueError ending in '(was C++ INVALID_ARGUMENT)' gives that code and the message before the suffix
a RuntimeError or an AttributeError with no hidden status gives ('UNKNOWN', its own message)

origin.section: A Refusal Is Raised as an AttributeError in OR-Tools 9.15, and Its Reason Is on __context__

concepts: in OR-Tools 9.15 a refusal arrives as an AttributeError whose __context__ carries the status code and message
